_ab_experiments.description: Example: onboarding experiment against the synthetic seed dataset

_ab_results.metric_query:
{% import 'abkit_assignment.jinja' as ab %}
-- CUPED needs no extra SQL: with covariate_lookback set on the method,
-- abkit renders THIS SAME query a second time over the pre-period window
-- (exposure filter dropped) and uses the pre-period value as the covariate.
SELECT
    {{ ab.variant_col() }}  AS variant,
    user_id,
    sum(gross_usd)          AS gross_usd    -- ADDITIVE: one row per unit
FROM {{ data_database }}.example_signup_events
{{ ab.exposed_units() }}
GROUP BY variant, user_id
_ab_results.metric_rendered_query:
-- CUPED needs no extra SQL: with covariate_lookback set on the method,
-- abkit renders THIS SAME query a second time over the pre-period window
-- (exposure filter dropped) and uses the pre-period value as the covariate.
SELECT
    _abk_exposures._abk_variant  AS variant,
    user_id,
    sum(gross_usd)          AS gross_usd    -- ADDITIVE: one row per unit
FROM analytics.example_signup_events
INNER JOIN (
    SELECT
        unit_id     AS _abk_unit_id,
        variant     AS _abk_variant,
        exposure_ts AS _abk_exposure_ts,
        stratum     AS _abk_stratum
    FROM (SELECT user_id AS unit_id, variant, MIN(exposure_ts) AS exposure_ts, NULL AS stratum, 'example_signup_test' AS experiment FROM (
-- The assignment (exposure) source: one row per unit with its variant and
-- first-exposure timestamp. By default abkit never persists this — every
-- metric query joins the LIVE assignment cohort via the packaged macro.
-- Set assignment.cohort_copy.enabled: true in the experiment YAML to persist
-- an incremental, append-only copy into _ab_exposures instead (worth it for
-- a heavy multi-join or a mutating source).
SELECT
    user_id,
    variant,
    exposure_ts
FROM analytics.example_ab_assignments
WHERE 1 = 1
) _abk_raw GROUP BY user_id, variant) _abk_cohort    WHERE experiment = 'example_signup_test'
) AS _abk_exposures ON _abk_exposures._abk_unit_id = toString(user_id)
WHERE event_date >= '2024-07-01'
  AND event_date <= '2024-07-01'
  AND event_time >= '2024-07-01 00:00:00'
  AND event_time < '2024-07-02 00:00:00'  AND event_time >= _abk_exposures._abk_exposure_ts
GROUP BY variant, user_id

dashboard_row.name: m14_2arm
rationale: CI excludes zero in the desired direction (up) at every informative cutoff in the trailing 7-day window (8 cutoffs)

params.description: Effect estimand: relative lift over control (default) or absolute difference.
params.name: test_type

params.description: Number of bootstrap resamples.
params.name: n_samples

params.description: Resample within strata (requires categories_array on the samples).
params.name: stratify

params.description: How per-stratum weights are pooled across variants (baseline §4.2).
params.name: weight_method

params.description: Named statistic bootstrapped per resample — a key of abkit.stats.bootstrap.applier.STAT_FUNCS ('mean'/'median' built in; extend via register_stat — names, not callables, so identity stays hashable). The Poisson engine is mean-only (H7).
params.name: stat

params.description: Bootstrap RNG seed. Identity-excluded for ALL bootstrap methods (declarative-config.md §7); the pipeline derives it per row via rng.derive_seed.
params.name: seed

params.description: Memory cap for the resample matrix; replicates stream in blocks under it (H10). Never changes results — block boundaries are stream-invariant.
params.name: max_block_bytes

params.description: Bootstrap p-value estimator: 'sign' = legacy 2*min(P(boot>0), P(boot<0)) (baseline-faithful default); 'plugin' = (#extreme+1)/(n+1) smoothing (H4, opt-in; ties at 0 count as extreme on both sides).
params.name: pvalue_kind

params.description: Effect estimand: relative lift over control (default) or absolute difference.
params.name: test_type

params.description: Compute per-arm MDE at the configured power (statsmodels solve).
params.name: calculate_mde

params.description: Target power for the MDE solve.
params.name: power

params.description: Pre-period covariate window (fixed whole-day lookback, e.g. '14d' — statistics-changes.md §5). IDENTITY-BEARING: a different lookback is a different covariate, hence a different series. The math here never reads it — the pipeline's loader materialises the covariate values; the duration grammar is validated by the config layer (the pure core does not parse durations).
params.name: covariate_lookback

params.description: Confidence-interval construction for the RELATIVE effect (m13 STAT-4). 'delta' (default, legacy parity) is the Wald interval effect ± z·SE with the variance evaluated at the estimate — a different test from the absolute p-value beside it, so the two can disagree about the same hypothesis. 'fieller' inverts the score test at every candidate lift: asymmetric, coherent with the absolute p-value BY CONSTRUCTION, exact coverage, and honestly unbounded when the control mean is not distinguishable from zero. Identity-bearing — opting in starts a new results series.
params.name: interval

params.description: Effect estimand: relative lift over control (default) or absolute difference.
params.name: test_type

params.description: Confidence-interval construction for the RELATIVE effect (m13 STAT-4). 'delta' (default, legacy parity) is the Wald interval effect ± z·SE with the variance evaluated at the estimate — a different test from the absolute p-value beside it, so the two can disagree about the same hypothesis. 'fieller' inverts the score test at every candidate lift: asymmetric, coherent with the absolute p-value BY CONSTRUCTION, exact coverage, and honestly unbounded when the control mean is not distinguishable from zero. Identity-bearing — opting in starts a new results series.

'pooled' (default, legacy parity) is effect ± z·σ̂₀ with σ̂₀ the NULL (pooled) standard error — coherent with the p-value but a valid interval only at zero. 'score' inverts the same statistic at every candidate contrast (Miettinen–Nurminen in its Farrington–Manning form): valid everywhere, asymmetric, inside [-1, 1], and coherent with the p-value BY CONSTRUCTION. metrics.query:
{% import 'abkit_assignment.jinja' as ab %}
SELECT {{ ab.variant_col() }} AS variant, user_id, sum(gross_usd) AS gross_usd FROM {{ data_database }}.user_revenue {{ ab.exposed_units() }} GROUP BY variant, user_id
